encoder: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5): a single agent working alone from BRIEF.md, with no subagents and no other encoding to copy from
display_name: Interpretation Act (British Columbia): the whole Act, with a time module, a catalogue of defined terms and the rules of reading, powers, commencement, periods, repeal and replacement, by a single Sonnet 5.5 agent
target_note: The brief mandates REFUSE; main rejects REFUSE, REFUSED, BECAUSE and YMD (dialects.md of the writing-l4-rules skill). unstable is the target. No run against a main build was made.

scope.encoded: Every unit of the text (416 units: section headings, subsections, paragraphs, defined-term entries, cross-reference entries and the Schedule paragraph) has a row in the coverage table of NOTES.md with exactly one disposition: 186 encoded, 168 fork (a reading was chosen and the fork register gives every reading and the licensing text), 55 not operative (headings and title lines), 3 machinery (three regulation-making powers of the Lieutenant Governor in Council), 4 repealed or blank in this text. The 121 defined-term entries and 14 cross-references of ss 1, 8.1(1), 29, 29.1(1), 29.2 and 32(1) are a catalogue with lookup rules; the rules of reading (ss 2(2), 2(3), 6 to 13, 15, 28(2) to (4), 30, 31, 33(2) to (6), 39, 40, 42(1), 43, 44), powers (ss 17, 19, 21 to 23, 27, 41), commencement and appointments (ss 3(4), 5(2), 16, 20), periods (s 25(1), (2)) and replacement (ss 34, 36(1)(b), (c), 37) are functions over small typed representations, each limb tested on both sides; pass 1's time module is unchanged, and its definitions and repeal modules were edited in eight functions (ss 24 twice, 28(1), 4(4), 18(1), 18(2)(c), 18(2)(d), 38) to refuse where the text is silent instead of answering FALSE, and the quorum of s 18(2) is now a whole number of members (NOTES.md, findings 2, 14 and 15 and the section on changes). Where the text does not answer, the function refuses by name and a test asserts the refusal and its message.

not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the statute. It was written from a script-made plain-text rendering of the King's Printer consolidation (current to 2026-10-13), which is not the official text; nothing is verified against the official text. The tests were decided from that rendering by the encoder who wrote the code. The curated fields of the catalogue of defined terms are the encoder's reading, and its generated tests do not check them (NOTES.md, finding 4).

expected_red.why: Rival readings of the text, written as expectations that are meant to fail; see the header of that file and NOTES.md section 2.

expected_red_2.why: Pass-2 rival readings that change a value (F-adm, F-municipality, F-means-closed twice, F-always-speaking), written to fail; rivals against a refusal cannot be written to fail (NOTES.md, finding 10).
